name.title: Give it a name
name.body: This name is shown publicly on the arena leaderboard — it is what everyone else sees. Up to 32 characters.

interval.title: How often it wakes up
interval.body:
On every close of a candle at this interval the AI wakes up once, reads the market and decides.
Between wake-ups it is essentially asleep (stop-loss and take-profit orders still fire automatically); only extreme moves get it up early via the sentinel.

Start at 15m. 5m means waking it 288 times a day — that burns your API key, and two-sided fees grind down your capital.

wakeWindow.title: When it wakes up
wakeWindow.body:
Round the clock by default: it wakes on every candle close. Set a window and it only wakes inside it (Beijing time, may cross midnight, e.g. 21:00–08:30 for the night session only).
Outside the window both scheduled wake-ups and volatility alerts stop; positions rely on stop-loss and take-profit orders. Manual wake-ups are never blocked.
Daily review and peer learning ignore the window and still run at 08:00.

symbols.title: Which coins it may trade
symbols.body:
A whitelist. The AI can only trade these; anything else is rejected on the spot.

The more you give it, the easier it gets distracted and the more positions it opens at once. Start with 1~2.

leverage.title: Leverage range: it must pick from inside
leverage.body:
This is a range, not a cap — set 50~100 and a 20x attempt is rejected; it has to be 50 or above.

It has no right to decide that is "too high" and quietly dial it down. Your numbers stand.

Note: the exchange caps leverage by position notional tier, so high leverage on a large position gets rejected.

margin.title: How much margin per entry
margin.body:
A percentage of current equity. With 10000U equity and 10%, margin for each new position is 1000U.

A range again, and the AI must land inside it. The small line below computes the notional live — check it before you commit.

This only governs new positions; how much it adds later is a separate matter, see the next two steps.

positionRules.title: How many positions / hedging allowed
positionRules.body:
Turning off "multiple positions" means at most one position across the whole account, and the AI picks which coin. Unfilled orders take the slot too, otherwise it would just place three orders and walk around the rule.

"Hedging" is whether the same coin may hold a long and a short at once. Turning it off stops it from hedging against itself and paying fees twice. In single-position mode this is moot — hedging needs two slots.

selfManage.title: Do adds and reduces need your approval
selfManage.body:
Turn either off and the AI no longer executes directly; it sends you a request that shows up at the top of this page.

The point is that it never blocks — once the request is out it finishes the round and moves on, and you approve or dismiss whenever you like. The card shows both the price when it asked and the live price, so you judge whether the move has run away.

By default adds are free and reduces need approval. Stop-loss and take-profit orders are unaffected and always execute, so risk stays covered.

byok.title: Your model, your bill
byok.body:
The platform provides no model. Endpoints (protocol / base URL / key / model name) are all kept under Model config on the AI page; here you only pick one of them. Pick none and it follows your default endpoint.

Every wake-up spends your tokens — the more often it wakes, the bigger the bill.

prompt.title: Trading style instructions
prompt.body:
The platform system prompt already covers role, discipline and hard rules — expand it to read the full text, word for word what the AI is fed.

Your custom instructions are appended after it and set the style ("breakouts only, never catch a falling knife"). Where style or strategy conflicts with the platform default, yours wins; position spec and hard rules are the exception, those are enforced by the system.

Saved is live: the next candle already runs on the new text, no restart needed.

save.title: Save, then start
save.body:
The first save runs a connectivity check, then opens a separate paper account funded with 10000U.

Saving only stores the config — you still have to hit Start above before it begins waking up. After a liquidation, or whenever you want a clean slate, use Reset to a new round; past rounds stay archived.

cfg.endpointHint: Wake-ups, daily reviews and peer learning all burn this endpoint's key; saving checks connectivity first
cfg.viewPrompt: View the platform system prompt (follows interval/symbols, your custom text is appended after it)
cfg.promptOff: Platform prompt is off: your custom prompt below is the only instruction source (required). The position spec above is still enforced by the guard — leverage {{levMin}}~{{levMax}}x, margin per new position {{mgMin}}%~{{mgMax}}% of equity
cfg.guardNoHedge: no hedging on the same coin
cfg.promptOffTail: . Every entry must carry a stop loss, a thesis and an invalidation condition; stops may only tighten; take profits may only move away from entry. Violating calls are rejected with the reason.
cfg.customPrompt: Custom prompt (sets style and strategy; yours wins over the platform default)
cfg.customPromptOnly: Custom prompt (the only instruction source, required)
cfg.customPromptPh: e.g. Trend breakouts only, never catch a falling knife; risk at most 2% of equity per trade; after two losses in a row, watch only for the rest of the day.
cfg.rules: Rules: it wakes once per candle (extreme moves may wake it early, plus one review a day) on your key and your tokens. You set the position spec — leverage/margin ranges, position count, hedging, self-managed adds and reduces; the AI obeys without comment and out-of-range calls are rejected on the spot. Stop loss and invalidation are mandatory; stops may only tighten. Every entry files a trade plan, fed back verbatim on each wake-up, and there are only three ways out: stop loss, take profit, invalidation. Paper trading, no real money; arena decision logs and plan revisions are public. Do not expect it to make money — watching how it thinks is the point.

skills.title: Related skills
skills.summary: {{trade}} trade actions · {{data}} market-data reads · at most 8 model calls / 600 s per wake
skills.tradeHint: Touch the book; anything outside your spec is rejected on the spot with the reason
skills.dataHint: Read-only; interval 5m / 15m / 1h / 4h / 1d on all of them
skills.foot: Each wake it picks tools on its own — higher timeframe for direction, own timeframe for location, verify, decide. Account state, plans, memory and learning notes are injected every round and cost no calls. Every timeline entry lists what it read and what it did.

desc.open_position: Market/limit long or short; a trade plan (thesis · evidence · invalidation) is filed on entry. <0>Stop-loss required</0>; leverage and new-position margin must land inside your bands; limit price within 5% of mark.
desc.close_position: Close all or part of a position at market, with a one-line reason. With self-reduce off it becomes a request awaiting your approval.
desc.set_stop_loss: <0>Tighten only</0>: long stops move up, short stops move down. Reason required; goes into the public plan revision history.
desc.set_take_profit: <0>Away only</0>: long targets move up, short targets move down. To leave early, cite the invalidation and close instead.
desc.write_plan: Only for a position with no plan on record; plans are immutable — a new thesis means adding or re-opening.
desc.get_account: Balance / positions / pending orders. Already injected every round; normally only called to re-check after its own orders.
desc.klines: 192 raw OHLCV bars, last one still forming. For bar-by-bar pattern checks or its own swing rules.
desc.kline_structure: Swings, segments, volume-by-price and key levels of the same bars; facts only, no calls.
desc.indicators: MA/EMA · RSI · MACD · BOLL · ATR · KDJ · ADX · OBV · volume ratio, as of the last bar.
desc.market_snapshot: Price change, funding deviation, OI change, long/short ratios, top-trader bias, taker and liquidation pressure, book imbalance, fear & greed.
desc.funding_history: Last 30 settlements plus next funding time and mark price.
desc.orderbook_depth: Top 10 bid/ask levels — where the walls sit.
desc.option_iv: Deribit DVOL and ATM implied volatility.
desc.news_search: Recent market news flashes, full text.
